editorial: Sri Lanka has distinct weather patterns across its north-east and south-west. For the route we took—Sigiriya, Ella, Mirissa and Colombo—we’d favour the drier season across the south and central highlands.

seasons.title: December to April
editorial: We visited in mid-March, by when temperatures were beginning to creep into the mid-30s Celsius in the lowlands.
If that is not your cup of Ceylon tea, December through February should be more pleasant. The trade-off is peak-season crowds and higher prices.

seasons.title: May to September
editorial: This period is better suited to the north and east, including places such as Arugam Bay. The south coast and central highlands can receive much more rain, so it is a weaker fit for our exact itinerary.

seasons.title: October & November
editorial: These transitional months can bring unsettled weather across much of the island. If your dates are flexible and this is a once-only trip, we’d choose a more predictable window.
